title: Affinity-driven prefetch strategy and conservative key-shaping runbook
creator: Maya Rivera
description: Goal: reduce per-token serving cost by combining an affinity-driven prefetch layer with conservative cache-key shaping and TTL laddering while minimizing user-facing regressions. We will build a recommendation engine that proposes per-prefix TTL ladders and prefetch thresholds, accompanied by an automated staged apply/rollback harness (micro-canaries + waterfall anneal). Focus areas: hit-rate estimation under sparse traffic, avoiding cache key fragmentation, and safe economic rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Recommendation engine produces per-prefix TTL/lane proposal covering >= 75% of top-10k prefixes by QPS. 2) Simulated shadow runs show <= 2% increase in tail latency and >= 8% reduction in token cost for workloads in canary cohort. 3) Automated rollout completes with automatic pause/rollback triggers firing correctly in two injected-failure scenarios. 4) Docs and runbook published in Console with example config and links to notebooks.
implementation_steps: 1) Sampling: snapshot prefix cardinality and tokenization distributions across last 14 days using stratified sampling. 2) Hit-model: implement a lightweight Bayesian estimator combining LRU-like decay and recent-window exponential smoothing to predict marginal hit uplift per TTL increment. 3) Key-shaping heuristics: canonicalize variable suffix patterns (IDs, timestamps) into bucketed tokens; generate candidate canonicalization transforms ranked by expected hit delta and collision risk. 4) TTL ladder generator: produce conservative ladder (base TTLs: 0s, 30s, 2m, 10m, 1h) with expected hit delta and confidence intervals. 5) Prefetch policy: derive affinity-driven prefetch thresholds per prefix using predicted marginal benefit * cost model; output batching suggestions for RPC/gateway. 6) Validation harness: shadow-mode replay with cost/hitrate/tail-latency delta calculation and anomaly detection. 7) Rollout orchestrator: micro-canary -> cohort expansion -> global, with automatic rollback conditions and manual override UI. 8) Instrumentation: add dashboards for hit-rate, miss-cost, token-savings, tail-p99 latency, fallback-rate, and prefetch failure rate.
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggers: (a) sustained increase in p99 latency > 10% or > 50ms absolute for 5 minutes, (b) cost per 1k tokens increases > 3% for 10 minutes, (c) fallback-to-hosted-model rate increases > 0.5% absolute. Rollback actions: immediate pause of the current cohort, revert TTLs/prefetch config to last-known-good, and run targeted shadow replays to validate remediation. Manual escalation path: SRE on-call notified, create incident, snapshot config and traffic slice for postmortem.
metrics_to_monitor:
- Prefix hit-rate (global & per-cohort)
- Token cost per request (pre/post)
- P50/P90/P99 latency for cached vs uncached paths
- Prefetch success rate and prefetch missed opportunities
- Model fallback ratio and error rate
- Cache eviction churn and key cardinality changes
- Applied config rollback counts and time-to-rollback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: aggressive canonicalization may cause collisions and degrade quality. Mitigation: conservative collision classifier that rejects transforms with >0.1% estimated misclassification or >5% hit uplift uncertainty. Risk: prefetch increases transient load on upstream model serving. Mitigation: throttle prefetch with token-budget per-node and async backpressure; prefer batching window expansion over raw parallelism. Risk: sampling bias leading to overfit TTLs. Mitigation: hold out a temporal validation slice and require cross-validated uplift before rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests for hit-model math and canonicalization rules, integration tests for the sampler, and end-to-end shadow replay against 14 days of traffic in staging. Two failure-injection scenarios: 1) upstream model latency spike; 2) synthetic prefix collision introduced to verify rollback. Must pass SLO smoke tests before any canary step.
notes: Design decisions: prefer conservative, explainable heuristics over opaque ML models for initial rollout to make debugging straightforward. The hit-model should give both point estimate and a 90% CI so rollout thresholds can account for uncertainty. We will expose an opt-out tag per-customer to disable prefetch for sensitive tenants. Long-term: evaluate learned policies that adapt TTLs per prefix with a probabilistic safety envelope.
